questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination on the basis of course selection and for economic reasons. In Amsterdam I had the opportunity to follow a very specific minor within the area of my academic interests. Furthermore it was an affordable destination with many social and cultural offers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall the exchange experience was amazing! But unfortunately the Netherlands had heavy corona restrictions, which affected the last two months of my stay quite a bit.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The university is very organized and everything you need to now will be send to you by email. In addition they are very easy to contact and they respond quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Someone waited for me at my building to give my keys and show me around. Otherwise I didn't get any assistance at the arrival but I was assigned a dutch buddy after a few days, who was super nice and ready to answer all questions. But in general everything I needed to know was provided by email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
In general it can be very challenging to find housing in Amsterdam. I payed a housing fee to the university, who provided me with a selection of university housing opportunities. I would definitely recommend future students to find housing through the university! It is way easier and overall not that expensive. In the beginning I met a lot of other students who didn't have a place to stay and ended up spending a lot of money on hotels. 

Future students should consider how much privacy they need. I lived in my own studio appartment which was nice, but it also required me to be more proactive when socializing in the introduction days. It was fortunately no problem at all! If you live at campus you should be prepared for a lot of parties - luckily off-campus students are welcome to most of the parties at campus. 

Future students who wish to find housing through the university should pay the housing fee as fast as possible since the rooms are given out according to when you payed the fee. Also when you get your timeslot for booking a room, be ready! The rooms are gone in no time.  

Another really nice thing about finding housing through the university is that you get a welcome package with the basic things you need (duvet, pillow, kitchen stuff etc.).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A lot of students live off-campus! It was easy to get to know people in my building and I ended up having friends from a lot of different buildings including people on-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy but a lot of people applied at the same time for rooms which meant that the website crashed and a lot of the rooms were taken. Originally I wanted a room on-campus but everything was gone when I finally got back into the website. Looking back though I was very happy with the off-campus room that I got, and I can't imagine living anywhere else.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I followed courses offered by the faculty of medicine, which meant that they did the registration for me, so the only thing I had to do was to email them. The application deadline for medical minors is very early compared to the other faculties, so be aware.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An exchange coordinator was available via email - very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted even though the exchange agreement was restricted to another faculty (science).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about the faculty restriction.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of teaching is more or less the same as in my home studies at KU. But the level of the other students was lower than I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my class we were 27 students and most of our classes were lecture-based. But in general the lectures were more interactive and they took place in a normal class room. In addition to lectures I also had practicals, site visits, two debate clubs and one journal club. The practicals included one time looking at bacteria cultures/bacteria techniques, MRI computer practical and scientific reading. The site visits were mostly at the hospital located next to campus. But we didn't have any lab in the courses I followed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Minor Cancer - Immunity - Personalized therapies (24 ECTS) 
Minor Literature essay (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend my entire minor! 

I am very interested in immunology, cancer biology and genetics and these elements were the core of my minor. 
The level of details was lower than I am used to but the minor covered many topics which gave me a broader understanding. In addition to the previously mentioned topics, the minor also included virology, microbiology, neurodegenerative diseases, advanced diagnostics, imaging and therapies. 

Of course it was a medical minor, which meant that some lectures were a bit too clinical.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trash tax

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I rented my bike through swapfiets which was very cheap (150 kr per month). Public transport is more expensive than I expected, but most of the time I just used my bike.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were many different activities offered to students. A big gym with lots of different activities like fitness, different ball games, dance, yoga etc. They also had a cultural club with classes in drawing, mindfullness, acting etc. 

I joined a gym that was not associated with the university, because I specifically wanted to do crossfit.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I bought a museum card which gave me access to a lot of the museums in Amsterdam. The gym I joined was amazing, but also quite expensive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has a lot to offer with museums, restaurants, shopping etc. But a lot of the cities in close to Amsterdam are worth a visit as well! Many students also go to the southern part of the Netherlands, Bruxelles or Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. The culture is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the dutch people in your class!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The canals are absolutely amazing for the atmosphere. I also really enjoyed the going out culture in Amsterdam! The restaurants and the cafes are always full (so remember to make a reservation).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Get a bike! 
- Be open and spontaneous 
- Enjoy your time there! Time flies...

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many of the smaller stores they don't accept mastercard or creditcard, so you should consider to get a dutch bank account.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I feel more independent and confident after my exchange. I got amazing friends and a second home for life (luckily not that far away).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living alone in a new country during corona with many restrictions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
